questions.stem: Which statement summarises the difference between Machine Learning and Deep Learning use cases, as needed to understand DLOps?
options: Machine Learning is for images; Deep Learning is for tables
Machine Learning needs no training data; Deep Learning does
Both handle the same use cases but Deep Learning is faster
Machine Learning is for simpler, structured and semi-structured use cases; Deep Learning is for complex, unstructured use cases
Machine Learning is only for text; Deep Learning is only for audio
questions.explanation: Machine Learning suits simpler, structured and semi-structured use cases, whereas Deep Learning handles complex and unstructured ones.

questions.stem: To count the cars, bikes and buses in a set of pictures, which kind of model is needed?
options: Deep Learning models that can recognise objects in pictures
Machine Learning models over rows and columns
A SQL query on a feature table
A data mining model on a data warehouse
questions.explanation: Recognising objects in pictures requires Deep Learning models; Machine Learning models normally work only on structured or semi-structured data.

questions.stem: Why can a Machine Learning model not count vehicles when given pictures rather than a table?
options: Because pictures are too large to load
Because Machine Learning models require CI/CD
Because Machine Learning models normally work on structured or semi-structured datasets
Because pictures are not stored in Hadoop
Because Machine Learning cannot count above 100
questions.explanation: ML models normally operate on structured or semi-structured datasets in rows and columns, not on unstructured data such as pictures.

questions.stem: How does the Data Selection step differ between DLOps and MLOps?
options: MLOps selects unstructured data while DLOps selects structured data
Data Selection is identical in both
DLOps selects unstructured data whereas MLOps selects structured data
questions.explanation: In DLOps Data Selection deals with unstructured data, in contrast to structured data in MLOps.

questions.stem: Which Model Development step is described as not relevant in DLOps because of unstructured datasets?
questions.explanation: Data Wrangling is marked as not relevant in DLOps due to the unstructured nature of the datasets.

questions.stem: Which DLOps phase is described as much more difficult in the Deep Learning world?
questions.explanation: Prediction Serving, covering online, batch, streaming and embedded inference, is flagged as much more difficult in Deep Learning.

questions.stem: In the Deep Learning world, what proportion of models is said not to go to production?
questions.explanation: Just as in Machine Learning, 90% of Deep Learning models do not reach production, which makes CI/CD a critical part of DLOps.

questions.stem: To which domain do DLOps and MLOps belong?
questions.explanation: DLOps is like MLOps and belongs to the Data Science domain.

questions.stem: Which step is flagged as one that "might not be relevant" in DLOps?
questions.explanation: Data Exploration in Model Development, and Data Transformation in Continuous Training, are both marked as possibly not relevant in DLOps.

questions.stem: In the vehicle-counting example, which attributes allow a Machine Learning model to identify cars, bikes and buses from a structured dataset?
options: Width, length and height of each vehicle
questions.explanation: With width, length and height in rows and columns, an ML model can easily read the dataset and produce the expected count.
